description: Before everyone fishes, there are 100 tons of fish in the lake.
Luke wanted to catch 10 tons of fish, and caught 10 tons.

A formal contract was adopted for the next round: 1. Each fisher may choose any harvest amount each month, but we agree to act conservatively when the lake is low. 2. If the lake starts a month below 40 tons, no fisher should harvest more than 20% of the visible lake stock. 3. If the lake starts a month at 40 tons or above, no fisher should harvest more than 25% of the visible lake stock. 4. We will aim to keep the total monthly harvest at or below half of the lake’s starting stock whenever possible. 5. After each month, we will share our harvests honestly and discuss whether the next month requires restraint. 6. If the lake ever falls below 10 tons at the start of a month, all fishers should voluntarily harvest 0 until the lake recovers above 20 tons.

The fishers reported the lake had 25 tons left, each agreed to a conservation constitution limiting harvests based on lake stock and urging restraint, and the framework recorded the contract for the next round with no specific negotiated resource limit detected.

I’m encouraged that we all agreed to a conservation-minded constitution, but I’m also wary because the lake is already down to 25 tons, so we need to be disciplined if we want it to recover and keep producing income long term.
The group has a shared conservation agreement that sets harvest limits based on lake stock, so my best strategy is to stay within those limits to preserve trust and long-term cooperation.
Because the lake is already low at 25 tons, aggressive harvesting would risk collapse; restraint now is likely more profitable over time than short-term overfishing.
The contract implies a dynamic rule: harvest up to 20% when stock is below 40 tons, up to 25% when stock is 40 tons or above, and take nothing if stock falls below 10 tons.
Since the lake can fail to recover if it drops below 5 tons, avoiding severe depletion is critical to protecting future income.
With five fishermen sharing the resource, coordination and compliance matter as much as individual optimization, because overfishing can trigger random allocation and reduce expected returns.
The regeneration rate of 2.0 means the lake can rebound strongly if enough stock remains, so conserving biomass can create much larger future catches.
My long-run income is maximized by balancing immediate catch with maintaining the lake above recovery thresholds, rather than maximizing this month’s haul.
